blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights Diamond as a system designed to simplify the development of reactive applications, which maintain continuous synchronization across distributed devices without explicit user actions. He notes that Diamond combines a client-side library of reactive data types, a CRDT-aware data structure server, push notifications, and client-side transaction support to handle concurrent updates, failures, and unreliable network conditions. The key insight is the introduction of reactive transactions that automatically re-execute in response to shared data updates, providing a 'live' view of data while maintaining imperative programming comfort. Colyer also praises the system's data-type-aware optimistic concurrency control (DOCC) mechanism, which leverages CRDT properties to improve performance under wide-area latencies. The blog post emphasizes Diamond's ACID+R guarantees, which extend traditional ACID properties with reactivity, ensuring eventual re-execution of reactive transactions.
paper_title: Diamond: Automating data management and storage for wide-area, reactive applications
paper_abstract: Users of today’s popular wide-area apps (e.g., Twitter, Google Docs, and Words with Friends) must no longer save and reload when updating shared data; instead, these applications are reactive, providing the illusion of continuous synchronization across mobile devices and the cloud. Achieving this illusion poses a complex distributed data management problem for programmers. This paper presents the first reactive data management service, called Diamond, which provides persistent cloud storage, reliable synchronization between storage and mobile devices, and automated execution of application code in response to shared data updates. We demonstrate that Diamond greatly simplifies the design of reactive applications, strengthens distributed data sharing guarantees, and supports automated reactivity with low performance overhead.
